raw_response:
I farm the same 20.8 mu the old way, wheat after autumn, then maize right after wheat comes off. I do not like making big changes. What feeds my family is what worked on my land and what I see nearby. Last year the wheat did well when I put a solid base fertilizer and gave water at the key times, so this year I will do about the same. Money is tight because some people in the house work outside and are not always here to help, so I will not chase the highest yield with too much fertilizer. But I also do not dare cut too much, because if the crop turns yellow or ears stay small, that loss is worse than spending a bit more. For wheat I will use saved or local seed, plow and sow in early October, put most fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts to stand up fast. If the spring is dry, I will irrigate about three times. After wheat harvest I will not waste time. The maize has to go in quickly, so I will use a hybrid seed from the dealer, do light tillage or direct sow after harvest, put fertilizer once at sowing and once when the maize is getting tall, and give one watering if rain is short. I will keep costs steady and aim for a safe harvest from both crops, not the fanciest one.
